words.definition: Great courage shown when facing danger, especially during battle.
words.example: The soldier received a medal for his valor after charging the enemy line under heavy fire.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'value' — a society values the brave courage its warriors show.

words.definition: Showing great courage and determination, especially in difficult situations.
words.example: Despite being outnumbered ten to one, they made a valiant stand to hold the bridge.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside is 'ALI' — picture Muhammad Ali, the brave fighter who never backed down.

words.definition: Not discouraged or frightened by difficulty, danger, or disappointment.
words.example: Undaunted by three earlier failures, she launched her fourth attempt to reach the summit.
words.mnemonic: 'un-' (not) + 'daunt' (to frighten): nothing can daunt you into stopping.

words.definition: Showing no dread or nervousness when confronting danger.
words.example: The fearless firefighter walked straight into the collapsing, smoke-filled building.
words.mnemonic: 'fear' + '-less' (without): literally a person carrying none of it.

words.definition: Showing brave, spirited determination despite facing tough odds.
words.example: The plucky underdog refused to quit even while trailing by twenty points.
words.mnemonic: Like 'lucky' with a P — a plucky person makes their own luck through sheer nerve.

words.definition: A person's strength of spirit and ability to face hardship bravely.
words.example: The grueling final exam truly tested every student's mettle.
words.mnemonic: Sounds exactly like 'metal' — someone of mettle stays tough as steel under pressure.

words.definition: Full of spirit, courage, and lively energy.
words.example: The mettlesome young colt bucked wildly and refused to be tamed.
words.mnemonic: 'mettle' (spirit) + '-some' (full of): brimming with fiery spirit.

words.definition: Brave and noble in behavior, or politely attentive and chivalrous.
words.example: The gallant knight bowed and draped his cloak over the shivering traveler.
words.mnemonic: 'gal' + 'ant': a gallant man tips his hat politely to every 'gal' he meets.

words.definition: Courageous conduct, especially in battle, or courteous, chivalrous behavior.
words.example: He was decorated for gallantry after carrying his wounded comrade across the open field.
words.mnemonic: Picture a tall 'gallan-tree' standing proud — noble, upright, and brave.

words.definition: Loyal, dependable, and physically sturdy, especially in supporting a cause.
words.example: A stalwart supporter of the club, he attended every match for thirty years.
words.mnemonic: 'stall' + 'wart': a wart planted firmly in its stall, refusing ever to budge.

words.definition: Brave, bold, and determined in the face of danger.
words.example: The stouthearted captain steered the ship through the raging storm without flinching.
words.mnemonic: 'stout' (thick, strong) + 'hearted': a heart too strong and thick to be shaken.

words.definition: Brave, bold, and persistent, especially despite being old or overlooked.
words.example: The doughty old boxer stepped back into the ring to face a fighter half his age.
words.mnemonic: Rhymes with 'mighty' — a doughty champion is old but still mighty and unbowed.

words.definition: Firm determination to accomplish a goal.
words.example: Nothing could shake her resolve to finish the marathon despite the torn muscle.
words.mnemonic: 're-' + 'solve': you are dead set on solving the problem, no matter what.

words.definition: The quality of holding firmly to a purpose and refusing to give up.
words.example: Her tenacity paid off when she finally passed the bar exam on her fifth try.
words.mnemonic: 'ten' fingers gripping tight — from Latin 'tenere,' to hold, and never let go.

words.definition: Courage and strength of mind in enduring pain or hardship.
words.example: She bore months of chemotherapy with remarkable fortitude and never once complained.
words.mnemonic: Starts with 'fort' — a strong fort withstands every attack, just as inner strength endures.

words.definition: Firm determination and courage that keeps someone going through hardship.
words.example: Finishing the marathon on a sprained ankle took real grit.
words.mnemonic: Think of gritty sand in your teeth — you clench down and push through it.

words.definition: Bold willingness to take risks or break rules without fear of consequences.
words.example: She had the audacity to correct the professor in front of the entire lecture hall.
words.mnemonic: Audacity sounds like 'a dare-city' — a whole city full of people taking dares.

words.definition: The quality of acting with confidence and without fear of danger.
words.example: Her boldness in pitching directly to the CEO impressed the whole team.
words.mnemonic: Bold text jumps off a page; boldness makes a person jump out of the crowd.

words.definition: Courage shown when facing danger, pain, or difficulty.
words.example: The firefighter's bravery saved three children from the burning house.
words.mnemonic: A 'brave' warrior earns a trophy — bravery is the quality that fills it.

words.definition: Showing the ability to face fear or danger without backing down.
words.example: It was courageous of her to speak up against her powerful boss.
words.mnemonic: Courageous hides the word 'rage' — turn that rage into fearless action.

words.definition: Extremely brave, in the way admired figures act during a crisis.
words.example: His heroic dash into oncoming traffic pulled the toddler to safety.
words.mnemonic: Heroic = 'hero' + 'ic'; picture a caped figure leaping into action.

words.definition: Great bravery and self-sacrifice shown in dangerous situations.
words.example: Medals were awarded for the soldiers' heroism during the mountain rescue.
words.mnemonic: Heroism = a 'hero' plus '-ism', a whole creed built on brave deeds.

words.definition: Full of energy, courage, and lively determination.
words.example: The underdog team put up a spirited fight until the final whistle.
words.mnemonic: A 'spirit' inside you fires you up — when it shows, you're spirited.

words.definition: Showing brave determination and a willingness to take risks.
words.example: It was a gutsy move to quit her job and open a bakery.
words.mnemonic: It takes 'guts' — that nerve in your belly — to be gutsy.

words.definition: A show of confidence or daring meant to impress, often masking fear.
words.example: His swaggering bravado vanished the moment the fight actually began.
words.mnemonic: Bravado sounds like 'brave' + 'show' — it's fake brave put on for show.

words.definition: Shameless rudeness or bold disrespect that ignores normal manners.
words.example: She had the effrontery to demand a refund after breaking the vase herself.
words.mnemonic: Effrontery pushes your 'front' (your face) forward shamelessly — right in your face.

words.definition: Loudly confident and rude in a hasty, thoughtless way.
words.example: The brash newcomer interrupted the meeting and insulted the veterans.
words.mnemonic: Brash rhymes with 'crash' — a brash person crashes in without thinking.

words.definition: Taking dangerous risks without sensible thought about the consequences.
words.example: It was foolhardy to climb the cliff during a thunderstorm.
words.mnemonic: Foolhardy = a 'fool' being 'hardy' (bold) — brave but genuinely stupid.

words.definition: Acting without care for danger or the results of one's actions.
words.example: His reckless driving nearly caused a pile-up on the highway.
words.mnemonic: Reckless = 'wreck' + 'less' care — no caution, so you cause a wreck.

words.definition: Done too quickly without thinking about the possible consequences.
words.example: Buying the car on impulse was a rash decision he soon regretted.
words.mnemonic: A skin 'rash' erupts suddenly — a rash choice is made just as suddenly.

words.definition: Ready to do bold or risky things without hesitation.
words.example: It was a daring rescue: she rappelled down the burning building to reach the child on the ledge.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside is 'dare' — someone daring takes every dare thrown at them.

words.definition: Inclined to take chances and seek out exciting, risky experiences.
words.example: The venturesome traveler skipped the guided tour and hiked alone into the uncharted valley.
words.mnemonic: 'venture' + 'some' — a person with SOME real appetite for a risky VENTURE.

words.definition: Full of bold, flamboyant adventure and dashing bravado, like a movie pirate.
words.example: The swashbuckling hero swung from the ship's rigging, sword flashing, and leapt onto the enemy deck.
words.mnemonic: 'swash' + 'buckle' — a swordsman whose blade goes SWISH and whose belt BUCKLE holds a cutlass.

words.definition: A shameful lack of courage when facing danger or difficulty.
words.example: Abandoning his wounded comrade on the trail was an act of pure cowardice.
words.mnemonic: Starts with 'cow' — picture a cow bolting from a shadow; that scramble to flee is cowardice.

words.definition: Lacking the bravery to face danger, pain, or difficulty.
words.example: It was cowardly of him to insult her online and then block her before she could reply.
words.mnemonic: Same scared 'cow' image — a cowardly person runs like a spooked cow.

words.definition: Easily frightened; lacking confidence and shrinking from anything bold.
words.example: The timid intern lingered by the door, too nervous to introduce himself to anyone.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'Tim hid' — shy Tim hid behind his mother at the party.

words.definition: Anxious or uneasy that something unpleasant may happen.
words.example: She grew apprehensive as the plane rattled and the seatbelt light blinked back on.
words.mnemonic: Think 'apprehend' — you sense trouble about to be caught, so you feel apprehensive.

words.definition: Feeling or showing dread of danger or harm.
words.example: The fearful puppy cowered under the couch every time thunder cracked overhead.
words.mnemonic: 'fear' + 'ful' — literally full of fear.

words.definition: Lacking courage; too nervous or weak to attempt bold things.
words.example: This climb is not for the fainthearted — the last stretch is a sheer thousand-foot drop.
words.mnemonic: 'faint' + 'heart' — your heart goes faint and weak when you're too scared to act.

words.definition: Lacking courage or firmness; easily bullied or pushed around.
words.example: Their spineless boss agreed with whoever had spoken to him last, so nothing ever got decided.
words.mnemonic: 'spine' + 'less' — no spine, no backbone, so you can't stand up for yourself.

words.definition: Having no courage or determination.
words.example: It was a gutless move to fire her by text instead of talking to her face to face.
words.mnemonic: 'guts' + 'less' — having guts means courage, so gutless means none at all.

words.definition: Wicked and cruel in a sneaky, cowardly manner.
words.example: The dastardly landlord shut off the heat in winter to force the tenants out.
words.mnemonic: Think of the cartoon villain Dick Dastardly — always plotting mean, sneaky schemes.

words.definition: An utter coward; a person with no bravery at all.
words.example: Only a poltroon would desert his friends the moment the fighting began.
words.mnemonic: Rhymes with 'buffoon' — picture a cowardly buffoon fleeing at the first sign of trouble.

words.definition: A timid, feeble person who is easily dominated.
words.example: The new manager was such a milquetoast that no one bothered following his instructions.
words.mnemonic: Say it as 'milk toast' — bland toast soaked in milk; a person as soggy and spineless as that.

words.definition: Whining and crying in a weak, self-pitying, contemptible way.
words.example: Stop your sniveling, wipe your nose, and clean up the mess you made.
words.mnemonic: 'snivel' blends 'sniffle' and 'grovel' — a runny nose plus whimpering pleas.

words.definition: To draw back suddenly with a small involuntary motion when startled or hurt.
words.example: He didn't flinch as the needle went in, though his knuckles turned white.
words.mnemonic: Break it up: FL + INCH — you jerk back just an inch when something stings.

words.definition: To lose one's nerve and shrink back in the face of danger or difficulty.
words.example: The raw recruits quailed at the sight of the tanks rolling toward them.
words.mnemonic: A quail is a tiny bird that bolts into the bushes at the smallest scare — picture it cowering.

words.definition: To recoil or grow pale from sudden fear.
words.example: Not once did the old soldier blench, even as shells burst just yards away.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'blanch' — your face goes blank-white the instant terror hits.

words.definition: To grimace or pull back briefly in reaction to pain or embarrassment.
words.example: She winced as the dentist's drill grazed the exposed nerve.
words.mnemonic: Rhymes with 'mince' — you mince your face into a small pained squint.

words.definition: To shake slightly and uncontrollably, often from fear, cold, or weakness.
words.example: His hands trembled as he tore open the envelope with the exam results.
words.mnemonic: Holds 'trem' from Latin tremere, 'to shake' — the same root as 'tremor.'

words.definition: To shudder or move unsteadily, usually from fear or a powerful force.
words.example: The villagers quaked as the volcano rumbled on the ridge above them.
words.mnemonic: Think 'earthquake' — the ground quakes, and so do your knees when terrified.

words.definition: To move with small, rapid shaking motions.
words.example: The rabbit's nose quivered as it sniffed the air for a hint of danger.
words.mnemonic: A 'quiver' also holds arrows — pluck the bowstring and it vibrates in a rapid blur.

words.definition: To shake suddenly and briefly from horror, cold, or revulsion.
words.example: She shuddered at the thought of spiders crawling across the attic floor.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'shutter' — a loose window shutter banging and shaking in a storm.

words.definition: To feel intense fear or worry about something expected to happen.
words.example: He dreaded the annual review with his notoriously harsh manager.
words.mnemonic: DREAD = Dark Red Emotion Ahead of Doom — the sinking feeling before bad news.

words.definition: A sudden, overwhelming rush of fear that shatters clear thinking.
words.example: When smoke filled the theater, panic swept through the crowd toward the exits.
words.mnemonic: From the Greek god Pan, who struck travelers with sudden terror in lonely places — 'Pan-ic.'

words.definition: To make someone feel afraid or less confident about attempting something.
words.example: The sheer height of the cliff daunted even the most experienced climbers.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'don't' — a daunting task makes you sigh, 'I don't think I can.'

words.definition: A feeling of distress and discouragement brought on by a shock or setback.
words.example: To her dismay, the last train had already pulled away from the platform.
words.mnemonic: Split it: 'dis' (undo) + 'may' — everything you hoped may happen is suddenly undone.

words.definition: To fill someone with overwhelming, paralyzing fear.
words.example: The sudden crash of thunder terrified the small child under the table.
words.mnemonic: Shares the root 'terr-' (Latin terrere, to frighten) with 'terror' and 'terrible.'

words.definition: To make someone so frightened that they cannot move.
words.example: The hiker stood petrified as a bear stepped onto the trail ahead of her.
words.mnemonic: 'Petr-' is Greek for stone (as in 'petroleum,' rock-oil) — sheer fear turns you to stone.

words.definition: To shock and horrify someone deeply, often on moral grounds.
words.example: The jurors were appalled by the cruelty described during the testimony.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'a pall' — the dark cloth draped over a coffin; grim news casts that pall over you.

words.definition: Struck with sudden strong fear or shock at something dreadful.
words.example: She stood aghast as the flames swallowed the entire east wing of the house.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'a ghost' — picture seeing a ghost and your jaw dropping in horror.

words.definition: Easily frightened or made nervous, tending to bolt at small disturbances.
words.example: The skittish colt shied away from every rustle in the hedgerow.
words.mnemonic: Think of a 'skittering' kitten — darting away nervously at the smallest noise.

words.definition: Anxious and shaky, unable to stay still or stay calm.
words.example: After three cups of coffee, his hands were too jittery to thread the needle.
words.mnemonic: 'Jitter' — like a phone buzzing and trembling as it vibrates across a table.

words.definition: Slow or reluctant to act or speak because of doubt or unease.
words.example: He was hesitant to sign the contract until a lawyer had read every clause.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'hes-it-ant' — an ant frozen at a fork in the trail, unsure which way to go.

words.definition: To lose steadiness or confidence and begin to fail or stumble.
words.example: Her voice began to falter as she read out the names of the fallen soldiers.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'fault' — hit a fault line and your steps and your resolve crack apart.

words.definition: To shake or tremble, especially when speaking or singing.
words.example: The old man's words quavered with emotion as he thanked the gathered crowd.
words.mnemonic: 'Quake' + 'waver' — a tiny earthquake running through your voice.

words.definition: Unable to settle on a course of action; wavering and unsure.
words.example: The irresolute captain changed the ship's heading three times within an hour.
words.mnemonic: 'Ir-' (not) + 'resolute' — the opposite of resolved, so no resolution is ever reached.

words.definition: Unable to make choices quickly or firmly.
words.example: So indecisive at the menu, he finally let the waiter order for him.
words.mnemonic: 'In-' (not) + 'decisive' — you can never cut cleanly through to an answer.

words.definition: Boldly refusing to obey or showing open resistance to authority.
words.example: The prisoner raised a defiant fist and refused to answer the judge's questions.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside is 'fie' — imagine shouting 'Fie on your rules!' at those in charge.

words.definition: Open refusal to obey authority, or bold resistance against it.
words.example: In an act of pure defiance, the workers walked out despite the ban on strikes.
words.mnemonic: The raised-fist state of 'defy' plus '-ance' — the condition of defying orders.

words.definition: Not showing fear or hesitation when facing danger or difficulty.
words.example: She gave an unflinching account of the abuse, meeting every eye in the room.
words.mnemonic: 'Un-' + 'flinch' — you do NOT flinch, even as the blow comes at you.

words.definition: Steady and firm, not weakening or changing in purpose.
words.example: Through every setback, his unwavering support kept the whole team together.
words.mnemonic: 'Un-' + 'waver' — the compass needle that never drifts off its mark.

words.definition: Showing great courage, especially in battle or danger.
words.example: The valorous knight charged the gate alone while the others fled the field.
words.mnemonic: Built from 'valor' — a valorous hero is simply brimming with valor.

words.definition: Spirited courage and determination in the face of difficulty.
words.example: It took real pluck for the smallest boy to stand up to the schoolyard bullies.
words.mnemonic: Picture 'plucking' up your guts — reaching in and grabbing courage from your core.

words.definition: Bold energy, nerve, and know-how in tackling challenges.
words.example: The rookie had the moxie to pitch her wild idea straight to the CEO.
words.mnemonic: Moxie was a fizzy old soda — imagine gulping it down for an instant jolt of nerve.

words.definition: Bold initiative combined with common sense and the drive to get things done.
words.example: When the shop flooded, she had the gumption to reroute every delivery before her boss even woke up.
words.mnemonic: Say it as 'GUMP-shun' — picture Forrest Gump, who just started running and never quit.

words.definition: Feisty courage and spirited determination in the face of difficulty.
words.example: The smallest kid on the roster played with such spunk that bigger opponents kept underestimating him.
words.mnemonic: Rhymes with 'punk' — a scrappy little punk kid who's all fight and won't back down.

words.definition: Lively energy and enthusiasm, especially in creative or artistic expression.
words.example: She attacked the final movement with such verve that the whole audience leapt to its feet.
words.mnemonic: 'Verve' sits one letter from 'nerve' — think of a live wire, all V for vitality, crackling with charge.

words.definition: Flamboyant, confident flair in style, manner, or performance.
words.example: He looped the crimson scarf around his neck and swept into the gallery with unmistakable panache.
words.mnemonic: Originally French for the feather plume on a hat — picture a musketeer's showy feathered cap worn with a swagger.

words.definition: Dismissive or offhand about matters that actually deserve serious attention.
words.example: His cavalier shrug at the safety briefing alarmed the interns who had to work beside the machinery.
words.mnemonic: A 'cavalier' was a knight on horseback — riding up high, looking down haughtily on everyone below.

words.definition: Cheerfully carefree, often without proper regard for the consequences.
words.example: With blithe disregard for the storm warnings, the two of them pushed their little boat out to sea.
words.mnemonic: 'Blithe' sounds like 'blithe → blissful' — floating along in bliss, not a worry in sight.

words.definition: Appearing calmly unconcerned or coolly indifferent about something.
words.example: He gave a nonchalant shrug when told he'd won the lottery, as though it happened every Tuesday.
words.mnemonic: From French 'non' + 'chaloir' (to grow warm) — literally 'not heated up.' Stay cool, never 'chalant.'

words.definition: Lightheartedly free of worry or care; casually untroubled.
words.example: She strolled past the shouting crowd with an insouciant little smile, utterly untroubled by the noise.
words.mnemonic: French 'in-' (not) + 'soucier' (to worry) — 'no soucis,' no worries. Say 'in-SUE-see-ant': not gonna sue, not bothered.

words.definition: Staying calm and composed no matter how stressful the situation becomes.
words.example: As the engines coughed and died, the pilot stayed unflappable and calmly talked the crew through the landing.
words.mnemonic: 'Un-flap-able' — a bird whose wings never flap in panic; nothing on earth makes it flap.

words.definition: To give someone the confidence or courage to act.
words.example: The crowd's roar emboldened her to march up and demand a straight answer from the mayor.
words.mnemonic: Read it as 'em-BOLD-en' — to put 'bold' inside a person, making them bold.

words.definition: To brace or prepare oneself for a difficult or dangerous effort.
words.example: As the first snow fell, the villagers girded themselves for a long, brutal winter.
words.mnemonic: Old sense: to belt a sword around your waist. Knights would 'gird their loins' before charging into battle.
